scope: Retained Android-compatible accounts and inspected official Android registration lifecycle

sourceReview.signInAuthDecryption: Official LoginUtils decrypts SignInOutput.auth with the retained private RSA key and stores the result directly.
sourceReview.v6Transition: The official transition selects API version 6 and clears the public key while retaining the private signing key.
sourceReview.registerDeviceSuccess: The inspected success callback updates local device notification/version state; no auth rotation was found.
sourceReview.requestProfile: The current native client package, platform and version match the inspected Android profile.
sourceReview.deviceIdentifierDifference: The official application uses Android ID with a build-derived fallback; the desktop compatibility client uses a persistent generated identifier. This difference has not been shown to cause the failure.

conclusion: Correct native WebSocket setup alone did not resolve the protected API rejection. No proven auth-normalization or package mismatch was found. Do not rewrite retained identities or declare the session remotely revoked on this evidence.
privacy: No account identifiers, device identifiers, credentials, keys, raw responses or private URLs.
